text.p: Blue-chip stocks extended their winning streak Thursday, sending the Dow Jones industrial average further into record ground as tame economic data sparked a rally in the bond market.
At 1 p.m. EDT, the Dow Jones industrial average was up 24.22 points at 6,045.03 after closing Wednesday at a record high of 6,020.81.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 12-8 on active volume of 285 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
In the Treasury market, the 30-year Treasury bond was up nearly half a point, lowering its yield to 6.82 percent from 6.86 percent late Wednesday.

Analysts said financial markets were buoyed by news that construction starts on new homes and apartments in September posted their biggest drop in 21 months, falling 6 percent to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 1.438 million.
Building permits, a precursor of housing starts, were down 2.9 percent, indicating that starts would remain soft over the next two or three months.
Also, production by the nation's mines, factories and utilities grew more slowly in September, partly because of a continued slowdown in the auto industry.

Total industrial output increased 0.2 percent last month after a revised 0.4 percent rise in August, as businesses eased back to 83.3 percent of their maximum operating capacity in September from 83.4 percent.
While welcomed in financial markets, the data, however, encouraged fears that the slowing of the economy could go too far and take a bite out of earnings next year.
Michael Metz, chief investment strategist at Oppenheimer & Co. said that even if investors were not concerned about next year's earnings, they should be.

"The argument being used now is that the soft landing is laying the groundwork for an extended business cycle and that if you have a quarter or two of weak growth (that) removes inflation pressure and will dissuade the Federal Reserve from tightening," he said.
Metz said he did not believe the slowdown was very significant and that the future still held the prospects of wage and commodity inflation.
Analysts said the Dow index had to settle in now that it had forged ahead into the unexplored territory above the 6,000 level. It closed above that mark for the first time Monday.
Among special situations, TCSI Corp. was down 5-5/8 at 7-1/4 after reporting a third quarter loss.
Schlumberger Ltd. rallied 4-1/8 to 98-7/8 after posting strong results.
The Nasdaq Composite index was down 3.18 points at 1,247.81 and the American Stock Exchange index lost 0.04 at 576.48.
